after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The only eigenvalue of the system's matrix is $\lambda =1.$*
after.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

We are given that the eigenvalue is $\lambda =1$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}3-1 & 4 \\ -1 & -1-1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{w}_{1}+4{w}_{2}=-2 \\ -{w}_{1}-2{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the first equation is a constant multiple of the second. So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=-1-2{w}_{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get ${w}_{1}=-1,$ and therefore

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}-([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t-1){e}^{t} \\ (1-t){e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem in a Defective Case
content.problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The only eigenvalue of the system's matrix is $\lambda =1.$*
content.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

We are given that the eigenvalue is $\lambda =1$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}3-1 & 4 \\ -1 & -1-1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{w}_{1}+4{w}_{2}=-2 \\ -{w}_{1}-2{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the first equation is a constant multiple of the second. So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=-1-2{w}_{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get ${w}_{1}=-1,$ and therefore

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}-([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2t-1){e}^{t} \\ (1-t){e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ a\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ b\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}5-5 & 2 \\ 0 & 5-5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+2{w}_{2}=1 \\ 0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{1}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{1}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=0,b=\frac{1}{2},$ and $a+b=\frac{1}{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a System of Linear Equations in a Defective Case
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}b \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =-1$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-1+1 & 0 \\ 4 & -1+1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0 \\ 4{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$ we get 

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, we see that $a=0,b=\frac{1}{4},$ and $a+b=\frac{1}{4}.$

after.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}5-5 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0 \\ 4{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{4} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{4} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}]\,t{e}^{5t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3\,{e}^{5t} \\ (2-12t)\,{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}].$

Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
$v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda $ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $v$, the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

To find $w,$ we solve the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}5-5 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=0 \\ 4{w}_{1}+0{w}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
{w}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

The variable ${w}_{2}$ is a free variable. Setting ${w}_{2}=0,$  we get

$$
w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{4} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{c}_{2}}{4} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}]t{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -12\end{aligned}]\,t{e}^{5t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3\,{e}^{5t} \\ (2-12t)\,{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
